title: Machine learning uses historical warming patterns to constrain future climate projections
summary: A CatBoost model trained on CMIP6 simulations used the observed 1971–2020 grid-cell warming pattern to identify tropical and polar regions that best constrain later global warming. Applying these spatial constraints reduced projection error variance by about 70%, compared with about 48% using global-mean warming alone; the results depend on model-based emergent relationships and are projections rather than direct observations of future climate.
organization: East China Normal University; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium; University of Victoria

evidence.tested: A CatBoost model trained on CMIP6 simulations used the observed 1971–2020 grid-cell warming pattern to identify tropical and polar regions that best constrain later global warming.
evidence.unknown: The study is a climate-model emergent-constraint analysis; uncertainty reduction was assessed with leave-one-model-out cross-validation, not by validating future outcomes. The reported probabilities are scenario-conditional projections.
evidence.ai_role: Learned grid-cell-scale relationships between historical warming fields and future global mean warming across CMIP6 simulations, then ranked grid cells by their influence on constrained projections.
